title: DSC 10 AI Tutor
tech: React, TypeScript, Python, Tornado, Gemini | UC San Diego
summary: An AI tutor that lives inside JupyterLab, reads each student's live notebook, and guides them Socratically. Used by ~400 students across 88K sessions.
description: A full-stack JupyterLab extension that puts an AI tutor right next to students' notebooks in DSC 10 at UC San Diego. The tutor reads the live notebook, including the active cell, the lab instructions, and outputs, so its answers are grounded in what the student is working on. A retrieval layer surfaces relevant lecture examples using TF-IDF with Gemini reranking, and the tutor uses Socratic prompting that sticks to course-specific tools like babypandas, with an exam mode and topic-based practice. It has been used by around 400 students across 2 quarters, with around 88,000 tutoring sessions logged.

title: IDX Exchange Home Valuation Model
tech: Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, CoreLogic Trestle API | IDX Exchange
summary: A random forest model that values homes from 125K+ real-estate transactions, cutting error (MAPE) from 20.9% to 0.85%.
description: A home valuation model built during my data science internship at IDX Exchange. I engineered more than 50 features from 125,542 real-estate transaction records pulled from the CoreLogic Trestle API, using exploratory analysis to isolate the main price drivers. I then trained and tuned linear regression, random forest, and XGBoost models, reducing MAPE from 20.9% to 0.85% by log-transforming price and pruning low-value features. The final random forest model uses 16 variables and reaches an R² of 0.86. I presented results weekly to senior data scientists and documented the pipeline with reproducibility standards adopted by the team.
